question.text: Large Value Fund (LVF) schemes at Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund enjoy a specific exemption regarding PPM filing. That exemption is:

answer.text: LVFs are exempted from filing a PPM altogether.
LVFs are exempt from filing their PPM through a Merchant Banker or incorporating SEBI comments; they file under an 'intimation to SEBI' model.
LVFs are exempt from SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012.
LVFs must file their PPM through SIDBI instead of SEBI.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9.5 states: 'Large Value Fund (LVF) schemes are exempt from filing their PPM through Merchant Bankers or incorporate comments by SEBI, as these schemes are launched under intimation to SEBI model.' PPMs are filed with SEBI along with a duly signed and stamped CEO/Compliance Officer undertaking. The Trap: Option A over-reads the exemption — a PPM is still required; just the MB route is removed. Option C wildly over-reads. Option D invents the wrong regulator. Note: The current LVF definition (page 396 of the workbook) sets the per-investor threshold at INR 25 crore. The separate INR 70 crore figure that appears on page 238 relates to a different PPM-template/audit waiver category and should not be confused with the LVF investor threshold.
